record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: What experimental strategies, beyond combining existing photon and electric-dipole-moment measurements in the small overlap of their parameter space, can measure and test the quantized couplings of a discovered QCD axion after the initial discovery?

evidence.quote: If the axion exists in this overlap region, higher precision calculations of the matrix elements can break the degeneracy between the couplings and the local DM density. It will be interesting to develop other strategies that can measure and test the quantized couplings after the initial discovery.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the QCD axion framework, the axion is a hypothetical pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson associated with a spontaneously broken Peccei–Quinn U(1) symmetry that solves the strong CP problem. Its mass m_a and decay constant f_a satisfy m_a f_a ≈ m_π f_π √(m_u m_d)/(m_u + m_d), and its dimensionless couplings to Standard Model fields — notably the axion–photon coupling g_{aγγ} = (α/2π f_a)(E/N − 1.92(4)) and the axion-induced nucleon electric dipole moment d_n ≈ (a/f_a) × (2.4(4)×10^{−16}) e·cm — are quantized in terms of model-dependent anomaly coefficients (E/N for photons, with the EDM coupling being model-independent up to hadronic matrix elements). Suppose the QCD axion has been discovered as the dark matter, so that m_a and the local field amplitude (set by the local dark matter density ρ_DM) are known up to overall calibration. The combination of a haloscope measurement of g_{aγγ} and an axion-induced oscillating-EDM measurement of d_n determines only the products g_{aγγ}^2 ρ_DM and d_n^2 ρ_DM, leaving a degeneracy between the quantized model couplings and the local dark matter density that is broken only inside the narrow region of parameter space where both signals are simultaneously observable (and even there only when hadronic matrix-element uncertainties are reduced).

Problem. Devise experimental strategies — distinct from simply combining axion–photon (haloscope) measurements with axion-induced nucleon-EDM measurements in their region of mutual sensitivity — that, after an initial discovery of the QCD axion, can (i) independently determine the local dark matter density ρ_DM in axions, and (ii) measure and test the model-predicted quantized couplings of the axion to photons, gluons, nucleons, electrons, and other Standard Model fields, thereby distinguishing among ultraviolet completions (e.g. KSVZ-type versus DFSZ-type) of the Peccei–Quinn sector.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open-ended research direction in axion phenomenology rather than a single mathematical conjecture. No definitive solution exists; multiple proposals (e.g., fine-structure-constant variation searches, axion–electron couplings via atomic experiments, multi-haloscope cross-correlations) are under active investigation but no comprehensive strategy has been established.
